title: Jesus, Thou Source of Calm Repose
description: Jesus, Thou Source of Calm Repose in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 244 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ All and in All”, where the book credits them to Urwick's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, thou source of calm re-pose, All ful-ness dwells in thee di-vine; Our strength, to quell the proud-est foes; Our light, in deep-est gloom to shine; Thou art our for-tress, strength, and tower, Our trust and por-tion, ev-er-more.

lines: Jesus, thou source of calm repose,
All fulness dwells in thee divine;
Our strength, to quell the proudest foes;
Our light, in deepest gloom to shine;
Thou art our fortress, strength, and tower,
Our rest in toil, our ease in pain;
The balm to heal each broken heart,
In storms our peace, in loss our gain;
Our joy, beneath the worldling's frown;
In shame our glory and our crown; —
Our comfort, 'midst all grief and thrall;
Our life in death; our all in all.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
